catalog_quote: 17. STRESS. As a rule, a stem in Mori (a fortiori a word) consists of two or more syllables. ... one-syllable words are in Mori, just as in Pamona, always proclitics or enclitics. They thus cannot occur independently nor carry their own stress. Only words of two or more syllables, then, qualify for stress placement. ... Stress in Mori is placed on the penultimate syllable, so that the language is missing an important tool for keeping oneself aware of the derivation of words formed with suffixes. For stress placement the same applies of enclitics, so that one says for example ambáu ‘carabao’, but with the emphatic particle mo: ambaúmo ‘a cárabao’; likewise mateómo ‘he is already dead’ ... da’iaópo ‘still’, and a fortiori: raháno ‘his house’, opuáno ‘its stem’, inia mámi ‘our village’, etc. etc. If there are four syllables, in general the initial syllable receives secondary stress. Howeve…

Supporting Mead 1998 p. 97 and Mead 1999 App. 3 (g) sentences also confirmed in copies we hold. (2) Deciding source is a full reference grammar (Esser 1927-33, 434 pp original / 528 pp translation) with a dedicated stress section -- the most extensive description of any Mori variety -- but its base dialect is Tinompo = Mori Bawah; Mori Atas is covered by Esser's explicit scoping plus Mead's family-wide statement, not by a Mori Atas-specific description, because none exists (Glottolog: 6 refs, Glottolog's most extensive description = wordlist, verified today). sources.quote: 'Primary stress falls on the penultimate syllable of any simple phrase ... me'ene daylight, mee'neno the next day, lu'mako to go, lumako'aku I go. There are three exceptions ... the monosyllabic particles ke and ma ... always receive primary stress. The third exception is the sequence ...(C)VV+CV#, which optionally receives primary stress on the third syllable to the left of the word boundary.' Secondary: 'placed on the penultimate syllable of units of two or three syllables ... defined by either morpheme or word boundaries ... to the left of primary stress.'
